newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. State official casts doubt on casino bill.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. State official casts doubt on casino bill.

text.p: The chairman of the Empire State Development Corp, who said that Governor George Pataki was studying a task force report on casino gambling, said on Wednesday he was not confident that a casino bill would be approved by state lawmakers in 1997.

Asked by reporters at a Crain's New York Business breakfast about the chances of such a bill being approved by the legislature and by voters in a referendum, Charles Gargano said, "I wouldn't be as optimistic as you."

The official, who said he was not an expert on gambling and did not wish to take an active role in the issue because he had once served on the board of a casino company, said his informal conversations with state lawmakers showed "a negativity," about such a bill's chances.
However, Gargano noted that New York State is losing billions of dollars to New Jersey and Connecticut, which both have some form of legalized casino gambling.
One proposal for New York State would not allow casinos in New York City.
